newsitem.title: USA: Harris County, Texas, to sell $250 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Harris County, Texas, to sell $250 mln bonds.

text.p: Harris County, Texas, Commissioners Court Tuesday approved plans to sell roughly $250 million bonds in late October, Faye Christopher, the county's director of financial services, said Wednesday.
The negotiated offering is expected to consist of about $80 million of refunding bonds and about $165 million of new money, Christopher said.

The county plans to issue the bonds in late October for closing in mid-November, she said. Goldman Sachs & Co will serve as bookrunning senior manager, with Smith Barney Inc as co-senior manager, Christopher said.
The $80 million refunding, once complete, would give the county an additional borrowing capacity of about $650 million, she said.
The county currently has $2.7 billion of debt outstanding.
About $80 million of the deal's $165 million new money portion will go toward road improvement, Christopher said.
The remaining $85 million will be used for construction of a 20-floor criminal court building project called the criminal justice center, she said.
